content: Mumps is an infectious disease caused by the mumps virus. Chinese physicians generally believe that Chinese medicinal herbs can effectively alleviate the symptoms of mumps and reduce the duration of the illness. Herbalists typically design treatment plans tailored to the specific symptoms of each individual. The objective of this study was to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of Chinese medicinal herbs when used in combination with routine treatments for mumps. To achieve this, a comprehensive search was conducted across multiple databases, including CENTRAL (2015, Issue 1), MEDLINE (1948 to January week 4, 2015), EMBASE (1974 to February 2015), CINAHL (1981 to February 2015), AMED (1985 to April 2014), the Chinese Biomedical Database (CBM) (1980 to February 2015), China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI) (1979 to February 2015), VIP Information (1989 to February 2015), and other relevant databases of ongoing trials. The inclusion criteria for this review were randomized controlled trials (RCTs) that investigated the use of Chinese medicinal herbs for the treatment of mumps, with or without complications. Two independent reviewers assessed the quality of the trials and extracted data. In cases where data regarding participant allocation were missing, the reviewers attempted to contact the trial authors. However, some trials allocated participants based on their admission sequence, which is considered a pseudo-random allocation method. None of the trials included in the review concealed participant allocation or implemented blinding procedures. No eligible trials were identified for inclusion in this review. A total of 108 studies claimed to use random allocation methods, but 104 of these were excluded because the allocation methods were not genuinely randomized. The authors of the remaining four studies could not be contacted, and these studies were placed in the Studies awaiting classification section for further evaluation. In conclusion, no randomized controlled trials were found to support or refute the use of Chinese herbal medicine in the treatment of mumps. The authors emphasize the need for more high-quality randomized controlled trials to be conducted in the future to provide reliable evidence on this topic.
